proposed.sourceName: Malaysian Journal of Syariah and Law — Gelatin in Halal Pharmaceutical Products (Tukiran, Ahmad Anuar & Jamaludin)
proposed.paraphrase: Malaysian peer-reviewed study concluding that gelatin's halal status depends on proper Islamic slaughter of the source animal, and that istihalah does not render gelatin from impermissible/non-Islamically-slaughtered sources halal because its chemical substances remain unchanged.

proposed.sourceName: Heliyon — Towards halal pharmaceutical: Exploring alternatives to animal-based ingredients (Herdiana et al.)
proposed.paraphrase: Peer-reviewed review stating gelatin is collagen-derived from pig and bovine tissue and that halal certification is essential for gelatin from non-halal animals; gelatin from animals not slaughtered according to Islamic law is not permissible absent halal certification.

researcherNote: Hanafi-strict position (governing bodies JAKIM/MUI/ESMA) reflects the strict juristic view that rejects istihalah for gelatin. Both peer-reviewed sources independently support a non-halal grade for non-zabiha animal gelatin, matching seeded draft grade 4 (Questionable - widely avoided). High-traffic -> two INDEPENDENT tier-2 sources (distinct authors/journals). APPROVED by owner 2026-06-28.
